etching-035.summary: The explanation attributes the negative DC self-bias of a capacitively coupled electrode solely to electrons being more mobile than ions, and states it as holding for any such electrode. The condition that actually produces a nonzero DC self-bias, namely the powered (wafer) electrode being smaller in area than the grounded electrode/walls, is missing; without it the statement is false.
etching-035.basis: Electron/ion mobility difference makes every RF sheath rectifying, so each surface sits negative relative to the plasma on time average. The DC voltage that builds up across the blocking capacitor (the self-bias measured from ground) comes from the asymmetry of the two sheaths: by the Koenig-Maissel area relation V1/V2 = (A2/A1)^q (q ~ 1-4), the smaller electrode gets the larger sheath voltage. For a symmetric discharge (equal electrode areas) the DC self-bias is zero even though electrons are still far more mobile (Lieberman & Lichtenberg, Principles of Plasma Discharges and Materials Processing, ch. 11, capacitive discharges / asymmetric discharges). Real etchers have a small wafer electrode and large grounded chamber walls, so the keyed answer stays correct; only the mechanism sentence needs the missing condition.

The fr text also violates the decimal-comma rule for French (guideline section 4). nl: "aftasten" means to scan/probe, not to remove material; the distractor describes SIMS sputtering, so use "afgesputterd" (full choices array given; only item 2 changes).

metrology-036.summary: The stress-to-Raman-shift coefficient "about 1 cm⁻¹ per 500 MPa" is given without the stress state; it holds only for uniaxial stress. For biaxial (in-plane) stress, the usual case for films and for many strained-Si layers, the coefficient is about 250 MPa per cm⁻¹, i.e. the shift is roughly twice as large.
metrology-036.basis: Standard micro-Raman calibrations for (001) Si (De Wolf, Semicond. Sci. Technol. 11, 139 (1996) and the literature it reviews) give roughly σ ≈ −(430–500) MPa × Δω[cm⁻¹] for uniaxial stress and σ ≈ −250 MPa × Δω[cm⁻¹] for equibiaxial stress. So the single value is off by about a factor of 2 for biaxial stress. Adding the condition keeps the existing 500 MPa value (valid for uniaxial) and makes the statement correct.

eda-047.summary: The worked example says that with a 1 ns period and 50 ps uncertainty the data must arrive by 0.95 ns, leaving out the setup time of the capturing flip-flop. The de translation additionally says "nach 0,95 ns eintreffen" (arrive AFTER 0.95 ns), which reverses the meaning.

Stating 0.95 ns as the arrival deadline misidentifies the quantity. This matches the glossary entry クロックの不確かさ (margin subtracted from the usable time). mosfet-022.summary: 解説が「厚さ0.3〜0.5 nm程度の空乏層ができます」としているが、0.3〜0.5 nm はポリシリコン空乏層の物理的な厚さではなく、空乏層が実効的に加える SiO2 換算膜厚(EOT/CET の増分)の値。物理的な空乏層幅は約1〜1.5 nm。加えて繁体字訳では正解の選択肢が「等同於實際的閘極絕緣膜變厚」(実際の=物理的な絶縁膜が厚くなる)になっており、「実効的な」の意味が逆転して正解の文が誤りになっている。オランダ語訳は「1 nm台」を「enkele nm」(数nm)としている。
mosfet-022.basis: ポリ空乏層幅 Wd = Qs/(q·Npoly)。Eox≈5 MV/cm(1.5 nm で約0.75 V)なら Qs = εox·Eox ≈ 3.45e-13 F/cm × 5e6 V/cm ≈ 1.7e-6 C/cm²、Npoly = 1e20 cm^-3 で Wd ≈ 1.7e-6/(1.6e-19×1e20) ≈ 1.1 nm。SiO2 換算では εox/εSi ≈ 1/3 を掛けて約0.35 nm。教科書(Taur & Ning 等)でもポリ空乏化は「電気的膜厚を約0.3〜0.5 nm 増やす」と書かれており、0.3〜0.5 nm は換算膜厚の増分である。mosfet-048 の量子効果(SiO2換算で0.3〜0.4 nm)と同じ書き方にそろえるのが正確。zh-hant の「實際的」は actual の意味で、問題の主旨(実効的に厚くなったのと同じ)と逆。

mosfet-048.summary: 解説が CET を「物理膜厚より大きい電気的膜厚」としている。CET が必ず上回るのは EOT(SiO2換算膜厚)で、物理膜厚ではない。High-k 膜では物理膜厚のほうが CET より厚い(例: HfO2 3 nm で EOT 約0.5 nm)。同じ文の後半で EOT に触れており、比べる相手は EOT が正しい。
mosfet-048.basis: 量子効果とポリ空乏化はどちらも絶縁膜「以外」の部分に直列容量を足すので、CET = EOT + Δ(量子効果) + Δ(ポリ空乏化) となり、CET > EOT。SiO2 単層なら物理膜厚 = EOT なので元の書き方でも成り立つが、High-k では物理膜厚 > CET となり誤り。用語集(zh-hant の該当項目)も「CET は EOT より大きい」と書いている。英訳はすでに「exceed the physical EOT」と EOT を比較対象にしている(表現を整えるだけ)。オランダ語の「elektrische diktes」(複数形)も合わせて直す。

package-001.summary: The explanation lists gold, copper and aluminum wire, then states without qualification that bonding is done while heating to about 150-200 °C with pressure and ultrasound. That is thermosonic bonding, used for Au/Cu ball bonding. Aluminum wire is normally wedge-bonded ultrasonically at room temperature.
package-001.basis: Thermosonic ball bonding (Au, Cu) uses a heated stage at about 150-200 °C. Ultrasonic wedge bonding of Al wire, both fine Al wire and the thick Al wire used in power modules, is generally done at room temperature. The site itself (package-024) says wedge bonding is common with aluminum wire. As written, the heating condition is stated as true for every wire material listed.

reliability-013.summary: The explanation says the strength of the Weibull distribution is that it can represent all three bathtub periods with one (1つの) distribution. A single Weibull distribution (one m) has a hazard rate λ(t) = (m/η)(t/η)^(m−1) that only decreases (m<1), stays constant (m=1) or only increases (m>1). It cannot produce the falling-flat-rising bathtub shape on its own.
reliability-013.basis: The correct statement is the one the question stem makes: depending on the value of the shape parameter, the same distribution family can represent each failure type. The whole bathtub curve needs a combination of Weibull distributions with different m, as a mixture or competing risks. As worded, the sentence suggests that one fitted Weibull covers the whole life. The glossary entry ワイブル分布 (section 形状パラメータと故障の型: 「1つの分布でバスタブ曲線の3つの期間を表せる」) has the same wording and should be fixed in the same way. That is outside this question set and is not included here.
reliability-013.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

reliability-014.summary: The explanation attributes the 150–250 °C peak of stress migration only to atoms being mobile (原子が動きやすい中程度の温度). That reasoning would predict the effect growing steadily with temperature. The peak at an intermediate temperature comes from two competing factors: diffusion speeds up with temperature, while the thermal-mismatch tensile stress falls as the temperature approaches the deposition or anneal (stress-free) temperature. The EN text already says "where atoms are mobile yet stress remains high", so JA and EN also differ. Separately, the nl question says "door spanning in de bedrading". In Dutch "spanning" reads first as electrical voltage, so the stem can be read as "atoms move due to voltage, without current", which points toward an electrical effect. deposition-033.summary: States that for both sputtering and evaporation the mean free path must be longer than the equipment dimensions. That holds for evaporation (~10⁻⁴ Pa) but not for ordinary magnetron sputtering, which runs at 0.1–1 Pa (as deposition-015 itself says), where the mean free path is only millimetres to centimetres, i.e. comparable to or shorter than the target-to-wafer distance; sputtered atoms do undergo some gas collisions.
deposition-033.basis: λ = kT/(√2·π·d²·p). For Ar at 300 K (d ≈ 0.36 nm): λ ≈ 7 mm at 1 Pa and ≈ 7 cm at 0.1 Pa (glossary 真空蒸着 rightly says only that at ~1e-4 Pa the MFP is far longer than the source-substrate distance). Conventional target-wafer spacing is ~5 cm or more, so the "MFP > chamber size" condition is true only for evaporation (and long-throw sputtering at the low end). Fix keeps the point (vacuum reduces collisions) and gives the correct condition per method, using the 0.1–1 Pa range already used in deposition-015 and the glossary.
